subject: General Knowledge
description: Hindustani vs Carnatic, ragas, gharanas, vocalists

questions.stem: Indian classical music has two main systems — Hindustani of the north and:
questions.explanation: Carnatic — the classical music system of South India (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh). Hindustani — North Indian system, influenced by Persian and Mughal traditions after the 13th century. Dhrupad and Thumri are genres within Hindustani, not separate systems. Manipuri is a dance form, not a music system.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Trinity of Carnatic music' refers to three great 18th-19th century composers. Which name does NOT belong to this trinity?
questions.explanation: The 'Carnatic Trinity' — Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Shyama Shastri — all born within a few years of each other in the late 18th century in the Tanjavur region. Purandara Dasa (1484-1564) is separately honoured as the 'Pitamaha' (grandfather) of Carnatic music and codified much of its pedagogy; he is not part of the Trinity.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: A 'gharana' in Hindustani music refers to:
questions.explanation: A gharana — from 'ghar' (house) — is a hereditary school or stylistic lineage passed from guru to shishya, usually carrying the name of its founding town. Famous vocal gharanas include Gwalior (the oldest), Agra, Kirana, Patiala, Jaipur-Atrauli, Bhendibazaar. Tabla gharanas include Ajrada, Benaras, Delhi, Farrukhabad, Lucknow, Punjab. A composition is a 'bandish' or 'bhajan'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Dhrupad' form of Hindustani music is often credited to the patronage of which Mughal emperor and the famous musician:
questions.explanation: Tansen — one of the 'nine jewels' (Navaratnas) of Akbar's court, patronised by Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior and then Akbar. He was instrumental in popularising Dhrupad and composing new ragas like Miya ki Malhar and Miya ki Todi. Amir Khusrau (c. 1253-1325) is credited with origins of qawwali and the khayal form, and the invention of the sitar and tabla (by tradition); he lived long before Akbar.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which raga is traditionally considered a morning raga in Hindustani music?
questions.explanation: Raga Bhairav — early-morning raga, serious and meditative. Yaman — early-evening raga. Malhar (and its variants like Miya ki Malhar) — monsoon raga, associated with rain. Darbari Kanada — a late-evening raga associated with Akbar's court. Raga-time theory (samay chakra) is a distinguishing feature of Hindustani classical music.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2008, belonged to which gharana?
questions.explanation: Bhimsen Joshi (1922-2011) trained under Sawai Gandharva and belonged to the Kirana gharana, founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan. The Kirana style emphasises slow-tempo elaboration and purity of individual notes. The Patiala gharana is associated with Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan; Gwalior is the oldest vocal gharana; Agra with Vilayat Hussain Khan and Faiyaz Khan.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'seven notes' of an Indian classical scale are called:
questions.explanation: Swara — a musical note. The seven basic swaras are Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni (short for shadja, rishabha, gandhara, madhyama, panchama, dhaivata, nishada). Shrutis are the 22 microtonal intervals from which swaras are derived. Tala is the rhythm cycle. Alaap is the slow, improvised opening of a performance that unfolds the raga.
